primary.title: Divi's Labs Q2 Results: PAT surges 64% YoY to Rs 1,127 crore; revenue jumps 35%
primary.description: Divi's Laboratories reported a 63.6% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 1,127 crore for the September quarter of FY27 (Q2FY27), compared with Rs 689 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal.Revenue from operations rose 35.4% YoY to Rs 3,676 crore in Q2FY27, against Rs 2,715 crore reported in the year-ago period.The pharmaceutical company reported consolidated total income of Rs 3,770 crore for the quarter ended September 30, compared with Rs 2,860 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.ALSO READ: Tata Steel Q2 Results: Profit rises 16% YoY to Rs 3,700 crore, revenue up 11%; Noel Tata to retire as directorThe company reported a foreign exchange gain of Rs 24 crore during the quarter, compared with a gain of Rs 63 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.On a standalone basis, total income for the September quarter stood at Rs 3,735 crore, compared with Rs 2,806 crore in the year-ago period. PAT rose to Rs 1,140 crore from Rs 696 crore.For the half year ended September 30, 2026, Divi's Laboratories reported consolidated total income of Rs 6,907 crore, compared with Rs 5,389 crore in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal. PAT increased to Rs 2,029 crore from Rs 1,234 crore.The company reported a foreign exchange gain of Rs 17 crore during the first half, compared with a gain of Rs 102 crore in the year-ago period.On a standalone basis, total income for the first half stood at Rs 6,765 crore, compared with Rs 5,282 crore in the corresponding period last year. primary.title: Samir Arora backed Helios Mid Cap Fund adds Aurobindo Pharma, 2 others, increase stake in Paytm, MCX and 16 others
primary.description: Samir Arora backed Helios Mid Cap Fund has added Aurobindo Pharma and two other stocks in its portfolio in October and has increased its exposure in Paytm, Multi Commodity Exchange of India and 16 more stocks in the same period, according to the monthly portfolio disclosed on ACE MF.The fund added 2.54 lakh shares of Aurobindo Pharma in its portfolio worth a market value of Rs 42.74 crore. The fund added 11.77 lakh shares of Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses in its portfolio and this was followed by addition of 1.29 lakh shares of PVR Inox in the portfolio in October.The midcap fund added 27,200 stocks of One97 Communication (Paytm) in its portfolio taking the total count of shares to 5.10 lakh in October compared to 4.83 lakh shares in September. The fund added 51,430 shares of Multi Commodity Exchange of India in its portfolio and had 1.89 lakh shares in the said time period.Also Read | SIFs gain investor traction with over Rs 38,000 crore in assets. Should investors add them to their portfolios this Diwali?Among the other 16 stocks, the fund added the maximum number of shares of Ace Vector. The fund added 12.77 lakh shares of AceVector in its portfolio and had a total 47.77 lakh shares in its portfolio in October.This was followed by addition of 3.13 lakh shares of ITC Hotels in the portfolio and the fund had 11.17 lakh shares in its portfolio in October. The fund added 2.57 lakh shares of The Indian Hotels Company, 1.54 lakh shares of Gokaldas Exports, 1.05 lakh shares of AU Small Finance Bank and 86,600 shares of Ather Energy.The other 10 stocks where the fund increased its exposure were Siemens Energy India, Rentomojo, Bosch, Schaeffler India, GE Vernova T&D India, Radico Khaitan, Coforge, APL Apollo Tubes, Sona BLW Precision Forgings and 360 One Wam.A complete exit was made from Park Medi World by selling 4.89 lakh shares from the portfolio worth a market value of Rs 13.45 crore. The fund did not reduce its exposure in any stock.The exposure remained unchanged in 56 stocks which included some names such as Physicswallah, Swiggy, Delhivery, Billionbrains Garage Ventures, Cummins India, Marico, Piramal Finance, City Union Bank, Edelweiss Financial Services, Nippon AMC, and Bharti Hexacom.As a percentage of NAV, the fund had the highest allocation in Coforge of around 3.50%, followed by 3.44% in Paytm and 2.74% in Sona BLW Precision Forgings.In October, the fund had 77 stocks in its portfolio compared to 75 stocks in the previous month. The portfolio of the fund was spread across 23 sectors with the highest allocation in the finance sector of around 16.22%. This was followed by 15.76% allocation in automobiles & ancillaries, 11.21% in healthcare and 10.04% in the IT sector.The fund had an AUM of Rs 2,421 crore as of October 31, 2026. The fund holds 65.27% in mid caps, 2.98% in large caps, 27.75% in small caps and 4% in others.Also Read | Quant Small Cap Fund adds Jio Platforms and 4 others; increases stake in Adani Power, 5 moreLaunched on March 13, 2025 the fund has delivered a CAGR of 20.51% since its inception. In the last six months, the fund delivered a return of 6.75% compared to a loss of 0.85% by the benchmark. In the last one year, the fund delivered a return of 6.58% compared to 2.24% by the benchmark.The performance is benchmarked against Nifty Midcap 150 - TRI. articles.description: Samir Arora backed Helios Mid Cap Fund has added Aurobindo Pharma and two other stocks in its portfolio in October and has increased its exposure in Paytm, Multi Commodity Exchange of India and 16 more stocks in the same period, according to the monthly portfolio disclosed on ACE MF.The fund added 2.54 lakh shares of Aurobindo Pharma in its portfolio worth a market value of Rs 42.74 crore. The fund added 11.77 lakh shares of Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses in its portfolio and this was followed by addition of 1.29 lakh shares of PVR Inox in the portfolio in October.The midcap fund added 27,200 stocks of One97 Communication (Paytm) in its portfolio taking the total count of shares to 5.10 lakh in October compared to 4.83 lakh shares in September. The fund added 51,430 shares of Multi Commodity Exchange of India in its portfolio and had 1.89 lakh shares in the said time period.Also Read | SIFs gain investor traction with over Rs 38,000 crore in assets. Should investors add them to their portfolios this Diwali?Among the other 16 stocks, the fund added the maximum number of shares of Ace Vector. The fund added 12.77 lakh shares of AceVector in its portfolio and had a total 47.77 lakh shares in its portfolio in October.This was followed by addition of 3.13 lakh shares of ITC Hotels in the portfolio and the fund had 11.17 lakh shares in its portfolio in October. The fund added 2.57 lakh shares of The Indian Hotels Company, 1.54 lakh shares of Gokaldas Exports, 1.05 lakh shares of AU Small Finance Bank and 86,600 shares of Ather Energy.The other 10 stocks where the fund increased its exposure were Siemens Energy India, Rentomojo, Bosch, Schaeffler India, GE Vernova T&D India, Radico Khaitan, Coforge, APL Apollo Tubes, Sona BLW Precision Forgings and 360 One Wam.A complete exit was made from Park Medi World by selling 4.89 lakh shares from the portfolio worth a market value of Rs 13.45 crore. The fund did not reduce its exposure in any stock.The exposure remained unchanged in 56 stocks which included some names such as Physicswallah, Swiggy, Delhivery, Billionbrains Garage Ventures, Cummins India, Marico, Piramal Finance, City Union Bank, Edelweiss Financial Services, Nippon AMC, and Bharti Hexacom.As a percentage of NAV, the fund had the highest allocation in Coforge of around 3.50%, followed by 3.44% in Paytm and 2.74% in Sona BLW Precision Forgings.In October, the fund had 77 stocks in its portfolio compared to 75 stocks in the previous month. The portfolio of the fund was spread across 23 sectors with the highest allocation in the finance sector of around 16.22%. This was followed by 15.76% allocation in automobiles & ancillaries, 11.21% in healthcare and 10.04% in the IT sector.The fund had an AUM of Rs 2,421 crore as of October 31, 2026. The fund holds 65.27% in mid caps, 2.98% in large caps, 27.75% in small caps and 4% in others.Also Read | Quant Small Cap Fund adds Jio Platforms and 4 others; increases stake in Adani Power, 5 moreLaunched on March 13, 2025 the fund has delivered a CAGR of 20.51% since its inception. In the last six months, the fund delivered a return of 6.75% compared to a loss of 0.85% by the benchmark. In the last one year, the fund delivered a return of 6.58% compared to 2.24% by the benchmark.The performance is benchmarked against Nifty Midcap 150 - TRI. The fund is suitable for investors who are seeking long term wealth creation and want investment in equity and equity related securities predominantly of midcap companies.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. primary.title: Airtel calls for industry-wide data pricing reset
primary.description: New Delhi: Bharti Airtel Friday told analysts its prepaid tweaks are only a trial run, and that sustained growth in average revenue per user - a key growth metric - will need a sector-wide shift in how data is priced.Asked on the Q2 FY27 earnings call whether its August intervention was a step towards fixing the industry's pricing architecture, Shashwat Sharma, managing director of Bharti Airtel, said the problem was structural. The sector, he said, has "a very flat architecture and very low ARPUs.""You're giving away unlimited usage, and you're not monetising consumption in a way. Data in that sense is not charged properly." The withdrawal of the ₹299 plan move, he said, was "more of an experimentation on our own base to keep moving ARPUs up," while "the architecture correction is a much broader correction that is required in the industry."Airtel's India mobile ARPU rose to ₹271 from ₹264, helped by premiumisation and an extra day in the quarter. Sharma said the Q2 prepaid action had "already kind of paid out," with postpaid upgrades, international roaming and top-ups as the next levers.Data usage per user, an analyst noted, is closing the gap with peers to 20-odd percent. Sharma said heavy users must contribute more, "People who consume heavily must pay for data proportionately, and that is the shift the industry eventually will have to make." Doing so would give "organic growth of ARPU, which is consumption-led," and "a pivotal shift that we need to make."Sharma attributed higher churn to seasonality and tariff actions, which bring "a temporary impact on customer continuity." Interestingly, Airtel reintroduced the ₹299 plan that it had withdrawn in August, which had effectively increased the entry price for daily data plans to ₹349.

The fund added 11.77 lakh shares of Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses in its portfolio and this was followed by addition of 1.29 lakh shares of PVR Inox in the portfolio in October.The midcap fund added 27,200 stocks of One97 Communication (Paytm) in its portfolio taking the total count of shares to 5.10 lakh in October compared to 4.83 lakh shares in September. The fund added 51,430 shares of Multi Commodity Exchange of India in its portfolio and had 1.89 lakh shares in the said time period.Also Read | SIFs gain investor traction with over Rs 38,000 crore in assets. Should investors add them to their portfolios this Diwali?Among the other 16 stocks, the fund added the maximum number of shares of Ace Vector. The fund added 12.77 lakh shares of AceVector in its portfolio and had a total 47.77 lakh shares in its portfolio in October.This was followed by addition of 3.13 lakh shares of ITC Hotels in the portfolio and the fund had 11.17 lakh shares in its portfolio in October. The fund added 2.57 lakh shares of The Indian Hotels Company, 1.54 lakh shares of Gokaldas Exports, 1.05 lakh shares of AU Small Finance Bank and 86,600 shares of Ather Energy.The other 10 stocks where the fund increased its exposure were Siemens Energy India, Rentomojo, Bosch, Schaeffler India, GE Vernova T&D India, Radico Khaitan, Coforge, APL Apollo Tubes, Sona BLW Precision Forgings and 360 One Wam.A complete exit was made from Park Medi World by selling 4.89 lakh shares from the portfolio worth a market value of Rs 13.45 crore. The fund did not reduce its exposure in any stock.The exposure remained unchanged in 56 stocks which included some names such as Physicswallah, Swiggy, Delhivery, Billionbrains Garage Ventures, Cummins India, Marico, Piramal Finance, City Union Bank, Edelweiss Financial Services, Nippon AMC, and Bharti Hexacom.As a percentage of NAV, the fund had the highest allocation in Coforge of around 3.50%, followed by 3.44% in Paytm and 2.74% in Sona BLW Precision Forgings.In October, the fund had 77 stocks in its portfolio compared to 75 stocks in the previous month. The portfolio of the fund was spread across 23 sectors with the highest allocation in the finance sector of around 16.22%. This was followed by 15.76% allocation in automobiles & ancillaries, 11.21% in healthcare and 10.04% in the IT sector.The fund had an AUM of Rs 2,421 crore as of October 31, 2026. The fund holds 65.27% in mid caps, 2.98% in large caps, 27.75% in small caps and 4% in others.Also Read | Quant Small Cap Fund adds Jio Platforms and 4 others; increases stake in Adani Power, 5 moreLaunched on March 13, 2025 the fund has delivered a CAGR of 20.51% since its inception. In the last six months, the fund delivered a return of 6.75% compared to a loss of 0.85% by the benchmark. In the last one year, the fund delivered a return of 6.58% compared to 2.24% by the benchmark.The performance is benchmarked against Nifty Midcap 150 - TRI. The fund is suitable for investors who are seeking long term wealth creation and want investment in equity and equity related securities predominantly of midcap companies.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)If you have any mutual fund queries, message ET Mutual Funds on Facebook/Twitter. We will get them answered by our panel of experts. Do share your questions at ETMFqueries@timesinternet.in along with your age, risk profile, and Twitter handle.
